title: FDA RSABE, the VAL-FDA-HVD-001 scenario at a different seed and ten times the oracle count

oracle.arguments: power.RSABE(CV=0.31, theta0=0.90, n=36, design="2x2x4", regulator=reg_const("USER", r_const=log(1.25)/0.25, CVswitch=0, CVcap=Inf, pe_constr=TRUE), details=TRUE, nsims=1e6)
oracle.method_note: The same scenario as RSABE-002 at an independent Python seed and a ten-times larger oracle count. Its job is not extra coverage of the criterion but a specific question about VAL-FDA-HVD-001: whether the agreement that resolved it holds when the sampling error is reduced. A difference of definitions does not shrink with nsims; Monte Carlo variation does.

comparisons.tolerance_basis: DERIVED from THIS case's replicate counts, not copied from RSABE-002. 4 * sqrt(0.25 * (1/20000 + 1/1000000)) = 0.01428. Narrower than RSABE-002's 0.01549 only because the oracle side runs ten times as many simulations; the rule producing it is unchanged, and it was computed before the case was run.

DERIVED, one-sided. The R side computes this in closed form from the chi-square distribution of sWR^2, so only the Python side carries sampling error: 4 * sqrt(0.25/20000) = 0.01414 at worst-case p = 0.5. The oracle count does not enter, which is why this tolerance matches RSABE-002's rather than this case's other one.

not_cross_checkable: The overall p(BE), and the mixed procedure generally - as for RSABE-002.

Whether agreement at two seeds would generalise to every seed. Two seeds bound the sampling variation loosely; the systematic sweep across sWR and the three-seed reproducibility run live in validation/external/investigate_val_fda_hvd_001.py, whose evidence is frozen alongside the finding.
notes: Added by the VAL-FDA-HVD-001 investigation. p_be_pe is deliberately not repeated here: it agreed under both regulator settings and at both seeds, so a third assertion of it would add runtime without adding evidence.
